name: Taipei 101
headline: height
description: Taipei 101 is a 101-storey skyscraper in Taipei's Xinyi District, completed in 2004. Its stacked eight-storey modules flare outward like a pagoda, and a large tuned mass damper near the top counters sway from wind. The Skyscraper Center gives it a height of 508 m (1,667 ft), and it was the world's tallest building until the Burj Khalifa took the title.

measures.label: Height (architectural)
measures.note: Skyscraper Center height to architectural top, including spires but not antennas (1,667 ft)

measures.label: Height to tip
measures.note: Skyscraper Center height to the highest point of the building (1,667 ft)

facts.text: Taipei 101 has 101 floors above ground and 5 below ground; construction started in 1999 and it was completed in 2004.
It was the tallest building in the world from 2004 to 2010, taking the title from Petronas Tower 1 and losing it to the Burj Khalifa.
A 728-ton spherical steel pendulum, a tuned mass damper, sits in a multi-storey cavity near the top to offset wind movement.
It earned LEED Platinum certification for operations and maintenance in 2011.

sources.publisher: Council on Vertical Urbanism, formerly CTBUH (The Skyscraper Center)
sources.title: TAIPEI 101 - The Skyscraper Center

caveats: The Skyscraper Center database now carries the Council on Vertical Urbanism (CVU) name; its height categories are the CTBUH ones (architectural top includes spires but not antennas).
The Skyscraper Center gives the tuned mass damper as 728 tons without saying which ton, so it is not stored as a mass measure.
World rankings change as new towers are completed; the ranks quoted are as shown on the Skyscraper Center in September 2026.
